title: Obesity as a Risk Factor in Pediatric Sepsis: Α Retrospective Comparative Study Under the Phoenix Definition
content:
Objectives: The relationship between sepsis outcome and obesity has attracted a significant interest in medical community. However, this association has not been tested under a new pediatric sepsis definition- Phoenix criteria. 
DESIGN: A single-center, observational, retrospective study of pediatric sepsis patients from January 2014 to December 2019
SETTING: The PICU located within a tertiary pediatric center in the United States.
PATIENTS: Children less than 18 years old with the diagnosis of sepsis. 
INTERVENTIONS: Not applicable. 
MEASUREMENT AND MAIN RESULTS: 640 patients with the diagnosis of sepsis based on the sepsis-2 definition were identified. Within the cohort, 631 patients met the definition of sepsis under Phoenix criteria. Patients were classified based on the body habitus as underweight, normal, overweight, and obese. Obese patients had significantly higher mortality compared to normal weight group (p=0.029). More respiratory and renal dysfunction was also seen in obesity group (p=0.008, and p= 0.0008, respectively). No difference in the frequency of identified gram positive, gram negative bacterial, viral, or fungal sepsis was observed based on the body habitus. 
CONLUSIONS: In our cohort of pediatric sepsis, obesity was significantly associated with higher degree of organ dysfunction and mortality. However, no difference in the incidence of identified bacteria, fungal, or viral sepsis was observed.
